title: Inside an animal cell
note: An animal cell is wrapped in a plasma membrane and keeps its DNA in a nucleus. Membrane-bound organelles divide the work: the ER and Golgi build and ship, mitochondria supply ATP, and lysosomes and peroxisomes break things down.

items.ex: A phospholipid bilayer that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
Everything between the plasma membrane and the nuclear envelope: the cytosol and its organelles.
Holds the cell’s DNA as chromatin and directs protein synthesis.
A dense region of the nucleus where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosome subunits are assembled.
A double membrane whose pores control traffic between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
Ribosome-studded membranes that make proteins for secretion, membranes, and lysosomes.
ER without ribosomes; it makes lipids and steroids, detoxifies drugs, and stores calcium.
Stacked sacs that modify, sort, and package proteins and lipids into vesicles.
Double-membraned site of aerobic respiration, which makes most of the cell’s ATP.
Made of RNA and protein, they translate mRNA into protein, free or bound to the rough ER.
Holds acid-loving digestive enzymes that break down worn-out organelles and debris.
Breaks down fatty acids and detoxifies poisons, destroying the hydrogen peroxide it makes.
A small membrane sac that carries cargo between organelles or to the cell surface.
The microtubule-organizing center near the nucleus, with two centrioles at right angles.

title: Inside a plant cell
note: A plant cell has the same core organelles as an animal cell, plus a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole. It has no centrosome, and lysosome-like digestion happens in the vacuole.

items.ex: A rigid layer made mainly of cellulose, outside the plasma membrane, that supports and shapes the cell.
The phospholipid bilayer just inside the cell wall that controls what enters and leaves.
A large water-filled sac whose pressure against the wall keeps the plant firm; losing water makes it wilt.
The site of photosynthesis; its stacked thylakoids, called grana, hold chlorophyll.
Holds the cell’s DNA inside a double nuclear envelope.
Makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits inside the nucleus.
Plant cells have mitochondria too; they make ATP by cellular respiration.
Ribosome-studded membranes, continuous with the nuclear envelope, that make proteins.
Processes and packages proteins, and in plants also makes polysaccharides for the cell wall.
Channels through the cell wall that link the cytoplasm of neighboring plant cells.
